examples.ko: 글을 보내기 전에 틀린 곳을 교정했어요.
examples.en: I corrected the mistakes before sending the text.
I started exercising to correct my posture.
Could you fix the typos for me?

examples.ko: 교정할 부분에 빨간 줄을 쳐 주세요.
examples.en: Please draw a red line under the parts to be corrected.

examples.ko: 치아를 교정하는 데 이 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Straightening my teeth took two years.
After proofreading the manuscript, I sent it to the publisher.

explain: 틀린 것을 바로잡을 때 써요. 글의 오타를 고치는 일(校正)과 치아나 자세를 바로잡는 일(矯正)이 소리는 같은 '교정'이에요. 학교 운동장을 뜻하는 '교정'(校庭)은 또 다른 말이에요. 일상에서 말이나 행동을 고쳐 줄 때는 '고쳐 주다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I correct my posture while looking in the mirror.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 자세나 치아를 바로잡을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used for fixing posture or teeth.

phrases.en: My teacher corrected my pronunciation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀린 말소리를 고쳐 줄 때 써서 언어 공부에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for fixing wrong sounds, common in language study.

phrases.en: I set the mistaken part right.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교정하다'보다 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday expression than '교정하다'.

explain_en: It is used for putting something wrong right. Fixing typos in writing (校正) and straightening teeth or posture (矯正) are written with different Chinese characters but sound the same as '교정'. The '교정' that means a school yard (校庭) is yet another word. For correcting someone's words or behavior in daily talk, '고쳐 주다' is more natural.

examples.ko: 이 서류는 기밀문서라서 복사하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This is a classified document, so you must not copy it.

examples.ko: 회사 기밀문서를 밖으로 가져가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take the company's confidential documents outside.
Confidential documents are kept in a locked drawer.
Confidential documents were leaked and it was on the news.

examples.ko: 기밀문서에 접근할 수 있는 사람은 몇 명뿐이에요.
examples.en: Only a few people can access the confidential documents.

examples.ko: 기밀문서로 분류된 자료는 이메일로 보내지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not send materials classified as confidential by email.

explain: 밖으로 알려지면 안 되는 중요한 서류를 말해요. '기밀문서를 유출하다', '기밀문서로 분류되다'처럼 쓰고, 일상에서는 '비밀 서류'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Please keep secret documents in the safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기밀문서'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday word for 기밀문서.

phrases.en: If you leak classified documents, you get punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖으로 새어 나가게 한다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means letting them leak out; common in the news.

phrases.en: This material is classified as a secret document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류의 등급을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a document's classification.

explain_en: It refers to important papers that must not become public. People say '기밀문서를 유출하다' (to leak) or '기밀문서로 분류되다' (to be classified), and in daily talk also '비밀 서류'.

en: to be written; to be filled in

examples.en: Your name and address are written on the application form.

examples.ko: 이 서류에는 중요한 내용이 기재되어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: Important details aren't stated in this document.
Please check the date stated in the contract.
If it's written incorrectly, you have to write it again.
I thought it would be listed on the receipt, but it wasn't.

examples.ko: 정보가 정확하게 기재될 수 있도록 천천히 쓰세요.
examples.en: Write slowly so the information is recorded accurately.

explain: '기재되다'는 서류·계약서·신청서처럼 공식 문서에 적혀 있을 때 써요. 메모나 일기에 적혀 있을 때는 '적혀 있다', '쓰여 있다'가 자연스러워요. 서류에서 '기재 사항'이라는 말도 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: Please write your name on the application form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 문서에 적는 동작은 '기재하다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 기재하다 for a person writing on a document.

phrases.en: Please check the filled-in details again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류에서 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen on forms.

phrases.en: The price is written on the box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '적혀 있다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 적혀 있다 is more natural in daily life.

explain_en: 기재되다 is used when something is written in an official document such as a form or contract. For a memo or diary, 적혀 있다 or 쓰여 있다 sounds natural. You'll also often see the phrase 기재 사항 on forms.

dis.h: stated or listed in a document, formal

examples.en: I read the contract carefully before signing it.
The teacher checked the homework so strictly that I got nervous.

examples.ko: 물건을 사기 전에 성분을 깐깐히 따져 봐요.
examples.en: Before buying something, I check the ingredients carefully.

examples.ko: 검사원이 제품을 깐깐히 살펴본 뒤에 통과시켰어요.
examples.en: The inspector examined the product meticulously and then approved it.

examples.ko: 집을 구할 때는 깐깐히 비교하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When looking for a home, it's good to compare options carefully.

examples.ko: 엄마는 장을 볼 때 유통기한을 깐깐히 보세요.
examples.en: Mom checks the expiration date carefully when she shops for groceries.

explain: '꼼꼼히'가 빠짐없이 자세히 하는 것이라면, '깐깐히'는 작은 것도 쉽게 넘기지 않고 까다롭게 따지는 느낌이 있어요. 사람의 성격은 '깐깐하다'로 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The judge examined the documents meticulously.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깐깐히'와 같은 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 '깐깐하게'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '깐깐히', but '깐깐하게' is more common in speech.

phrases.example: 가격을 깐깐히 따져 보고 물건을 샀어요.
phrases.en: I weighed the price carefully before buying it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따지다'와 함께 쓰면 작은 부분까지 꼼꼼하게 비교하고 확인한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '따지다' it means checking and comparing even the small details.

phrases.en: I check my luggage carefully before leaving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 '꼼꼼히'는 빠짐없이 하는 것이고, '깐깐히'는 까다롭게 따지는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but '꼼꼼히' is about not missing anything, while '깐깐히' carries a picky, exacting feel.

explain_en: While '꼼꼼히' means doing something thoroughly and in detail, '깐깐히' adds a feel of being picky and not letting small things slide. For a person's character, people often use the adjective '깐깐하다'.

examples.en: I checked my answer sheet against the correct answers.
They are matching the photo on the ID to the face.
Sign after you check the contract against the original.

examples.ko: 두 문서를 대조하면 다른 부분이 보여요.
examples.en: If you compare the two documents, you can see the differences.

examples.ko: 숫자를 하나씩 대조했지만 틀린 곳이 없었어요.
examples.en: I checked the numbers one by one, but there was no mistake.
I will check the ledger against the receipts.

explain: '비교하다'는 둘의 차이와 같은 점을 보는 것이고, '대조하다'는 하나를 기준으로 삼아 맞는지 확인하는 느낌이 강해요. 서류, 답안, 숫자를 확인할 때 자주 써요. '무엇을 무엇과 대조하다'처럼 '-와/과'가 같이 와요.

phrases.en: Please check the two documents against each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 나란히 놓고 맞는지 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when placing two things side by side to check they match.

phrases.en: I'll check the name against the list.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-와/과 대조하다' 형태로, 기준이 되는 것과 맞는지 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the '-와/과 대조하다' pattern, checks against a standard.

phrases.en: Please compare the two photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대조하다'와 달리 차이와 같은 점을 모두 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '대조하다', it looks at both differences and similarities.

explain_en: '비교하다' looks at how two things differ and resemble each other; 대조하다 feels more like checking something against a reference to see whether it matches. It is common with documents, answers, and numbers. It pairs with -와/과: 'A를 B와 대조하다'.

examples.en: I rummaged through my pants pockets, but my wallet isn't there.
My father rummaged through the drawer and then took out his glasses.

examples.ko: 책장에서 책을 뒤적뒤적 넘겨 보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm flipping through the books from the shelf.
What are you rummaging around for like that?

examples.ko: 신문을 뒤적뒤적 넘기다가 재미있는 기사를 봤어요.
examples.en: While leafing through the newspaper, I came across an interesting article.

examples.ko: 동생이 옷장을 뒤적뒤적하는 바람에 방이 엉망이에요.
examples.en: My younger sibling rummaged through the closet, so the room is a mess.

explain: 물건을 찾을 때도 쓰고, 책이나 신문을 대충 넘길 때도 써요. 비슷한 '뒤적이다'는 동사 형태이고, '뒤지다'보다 손길이 가볍고 느린 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I rummaged around in my bag and took out a pen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사에 '하다'를 붙여 동사로 써요. 손으로 계속 찾는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 makes it a verb, showing someone searching with their hands for a while.

phrases.en: I rummaged through the drawer but it wasn't there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 이리저리 뒤져서 찾는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when searching for something by rummaging around.

phrases.en: I flipped through the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 읽기보다는 대충 넘겨 보는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like leafing through than actually reading.

explain_en: It is used both when searching for something and when leafing through a book or newspaper casually. The similar '뒤적이다' is the verb form, and compared with '뒤지다' it feels lighter and slower.

examples.en: They are investigating the cause of the accident thoroughly.

examples.ko: 계약 내용을 면밀히 살펴본 뒤에 서명했어요.
examples.en: I signed after examining the contract carefully.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 검사 결과를 면밀히 확인했어요.
examples.en: The doctor checked the test results closely.
If you look into it closely, there are problems.

examples.ko: 선생님은 제 글을 면밀히 읽고 의견을 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher read my writing closely and gave me feedback.
I'll decide after watching the situation closely.

explain: '꼼꼼히'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있는 말이에요. 조사하다, 검토하다, 분석하다, 살피다, 지켜보다 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요. 방을 정리하는 것 같은 가벼운 일에는 '꼼꼼히'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The team leader reviewed the plan closely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '면밀히'를 '검토하다'와 함께 쓰면 서류나 계획을 빈틈없이 따져 본다는 격식 있는 표현이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 검토하다, it means going over a document or plan carefully, in a formal tone.

phrases.en: The government is watching the situation closely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 어떤 일의 변화를 놓치지 않고 살필 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news to say someone is keeping a careful eye on developments.

phrases.en: I checked my homework carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '면밀히'보다 덜 딱딱해서 일상 대화에서 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday word with a similar meaning to 면밀히.

explain_en: It is similar to '꼼꼼히' but more formal, and goes well with verbs such as 조사하다, 검토하다, 분석하다, 살피다 and 지켜보다. For light tasks like tidying a room, '꼼꼼히' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 입장하기 전에 명부에 이름을 적어 주세요.
examples.en: Please write your name on the list before entering.

examples.ko: 학교 졸업생 명부에서 옛 친구의 이름을 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found an old friend's name in the school's graduate register.

examples.ko: 참석자 명부를 확인했는데 제 이름이 없었어요.
examples.en: I checked the attendee list, and my name wasn't on it.
A new alumni roster has been made.

examples.ko: 이 명부는 개인 정보라서 함부로 보여 줄 수 없어요.
examples.en: This list is personal information, so I can't just show it to anyone.

examples.ko: 회원 명부와 실제 사람 수가 달라서 다시 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: The member roll and the actual number of people didn't match, so I counted again.

explain: 사람 이름을 모아 적은 문서를 말해요. '명단'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만 '명부'는 공식 서류나 오래 보관하는 기록 같은 느낌이 더 있어요. 일상에서는 '명단'이 더 자연스러운 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Please email me the list of attendees.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명부'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 일상에서 더 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means almost the same as 명부 but sounds more natural in daily life.

phrases.en: I put the new member's name on the register.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 공식 기록에 적어 넣을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a common pairing for entering a name into an official record.

phrases.en: The membership register is kept in the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 모임이나 단체 이름을 붙여 어떤 명부인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group or organization is placed before it to say which register it is.

explain_en: It is a document in which people's names are gathered. It means nearly the same as '명단', but 명부 feels more like an official document or a record kept for a long time. In daily life '명단' often sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 회의 내용을 바로 문서화해서 공유해 주세요.
examples.en: Please put the meeting content into a document right away and share it.
If we put the rules in writing, misunderstandings decrease.
The team leader suggested that we document the work procedure.

examples.ko: 말로 한 약속도 문서화해 두는 게 안전해요.
examples.en: It is safer to put even verbal promises in writing.
There is still a lot of content that has not been documented.

examples.ko: 담당자가 바뀔 때를 대비해 작업 방법을 문서화했어요.
examples.en: I documented the work method in case the person in charge changes.

explain: 말이나 머릿속에 있던 것을 문서로 남길 때 써요. '기록하다', '정리하다'보다 공식적인 문서 형태로 만든다는 느낌이고, 회사에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: All the rules are put into documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 문서로 만들어진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something already put into a document.

phrases.en: Please keep important content in a document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to put it.

phrases.en: If you put the promise in writing, you feel safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중을 위해 미리 해 둔다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests doing it ahead of time for later.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in writing in advance

explain_en: It is used when you turn something spoken or in your head into a written document. Compared with '기록하다' or '정리하다', it feels like making an official document, and you often hear it at work.

examples.en: I arrange the books in order of height.
The students arranged the chairs in a circle.
I did homework arranging words in alphabetical order.

examples.ko: 사진을 시간 순서로 배열해서 앨범을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I arranged the photos in time order and made an album.
If you arrange the letters properly, it becomes a sentence.
I arranged the flowers by color and took a picture.

explain: '정리하다'는 깔끔하게 치우는 느낌이고, '배열하다'는 순서나 모양을 정해서 늘어놓는 느낌이에요. '정렬하다'와 뜻이 가까운데, 컴퓨터나 표에서 순서대로 맞출 때는 '정렬'을 더 많이 봐요. 단어를 순서에 맞게 놓는 문제에도 써요.

phrases.en: Try arranging the words in order.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배열하다'에 '순서대로'를 붙여 놓는 기준을 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'in order' makes the arrangement rule clear.

phrases.en: The books are arranged in Korean alphabetical order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 놓여 있는 상태를 말할 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form used to describe how things are already arranged.

phrases.en: I arranged the chairs in a line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 '일렬'로 정해서 늘어놓을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the shape of the arrangement is a single line.

explain_en: '정리하다' feels like tidying up, while '배열하다' feels like setting things out in a chosen order or shape. It is close to '정렬하다', but for putting data or tables in order, '정렬' is the more common word. It also appears in tasks of putting words in the right order.

en: to copy; to reproduce; to replicate

examples.en: The scientists' cloning of a sheep is famous.

examples.ko: 이 파일은 복제해서 다른 컴퓨터에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I duplicated this file and put it on another computer.

examples.ko: 허락 없이 책을 복제하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not copy a book without permission.

examples.ko: 그림을 똑같이 복제하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to reproduce the painting exactly.
I went to a key shop to have a key duplicated.
Someone cloned my card information.

explain: 파일, 열쇠, 그림, 생물처럼 원본과 똑같은 것을 하나 더 만들 때 두루 써요. '복사하다'는 종이나 파일을 빠르게 베끼는 일상적인 말이고, '복제하다'는 똑같은 것을 새로 만든다는 무거운 느낌이에요. 허락 없이 하면 법 문제가 돼서 뉴스에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This painting is a copy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원본이 아니라 똑같이 만든 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to something made to match the original, not the original.

phrases.en: Please copy the documents and hand them out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 파일을 빠르게 베낄 때 쓰는 더 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word for quickly copying paper or files.

phrases.en: Duplicate the file and keep it as a backup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원본과 똑같은 파일을 하나 더 만든다는 뜻으로 컴퓨터 쓰임에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making an identical extra file, common in computer use.

explain_en: It is used broadly for making one more exact copy of an original, such as a file, a key, a painting or a living thing. 복사하다 is the everyday word for quickly copying paper or files, while 복제하다 feels heavier, as if creating an identical new thing. Doing it without permission can be a legal problem, so it often appears in the news.

en: to be unsuitable; to be unfit

examples.en: This place is unsuitable for children to play.

examples.ko: 검사 결과 이 물은 마시기에 부적합했어요.
examples.en: The test showed this water is not fit to drink.

examples.ko: 그 일은 제 성격에 부적합한 것 같아요.
examples.en: That job seems unsuited to my personality.
I was judged unfit and applied again.

examples.ko: 규격이 안 맞으면 부적합할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the standard isn't met, it may be unsuitable.

examples.ko: 날씨가 나빠서 야외 행사는 부적합하고 실내가 좋아요.
examples.en: The weather is bad, so an outdoor event is unsuitable and indoors is better.

explain: '어울리지 않다', '맞지 않다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 공문서나 검사 결과에서 자주 써요. '○○에 부적합하다'로 쓰고, 반대말은 '적합하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '안 맞아요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: These shoes are not suitable for hiking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부적합하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 조금 덜 딱딱하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 부적합하다 but sounds a bit less stiff.

phrases.en: This job doesn't suit me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to say it in daily conversation.

phrases.en: This is an unsuitable place for a child to stay.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부적합하다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 명사 앞에 붙인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form placed before a noun to describe it.

explain_en: 부적합하다 sounds stiffer than 어울리지 않다 or 맞지 않다 and appears in official documents and test results. It is used as ○○에 부적합하다, and the opposite is 적합하다. In casual talk 안 맞아요 is more natural.

en: person who has completed a course

examples.ko: 이번 과정의 수료자는 모두 서른 명이에요.
examples.en: There are thirty people in total who completed this course.
We give a certificate to those who complete the course.
The list of completers was posted on the bulletin board.

examples.ko: 교육 수료자만 다음 단계에 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only those who completed the training can apply for the next level.

examples.ko: 저도 작년에 이 과정의 수료자가 됐어요.
examples.en: I also completed this course last year.
The completers gathered to take a commemorative photo.

explain: '졸업자'는 학교를 마치고 졸업장을 받은 사람이고, '수료자'는 강좌나 과정을 끝낸 사람이에요. 그래서 학위가 아니라 '수료증'을 받는 경우에 어울려요.

phrases.en: Please check the list of completers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과정을 끝낸 사람들의 이름을 적은 목록이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A list of names of those who finished the course.

phrases.en: They give a completion certificate to those who finish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 끝냈다는 증명서를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the certificate, not the person.

phrases.example: 과정 수료자만 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only those who completed the course can take the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 과정을 끝낸 사람이라고 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear which course the person completed.

explain_en: A '졸업자' finished a school and got a diploma, while a '수료자' finished a course or program. That is why it fits cases where you receive a '수료증' (completion certificate) rather than a degree.

examples.en: The book is being printed and comes out today.
The name was printed wrong.
It takes two days for the poster to be printed.
The date is printed on the ticket.
Please check the printed document.
The file wouldn't print, so I checked the printer.

explain: 종이나 물건 위에 글자가 찍힐 때 그 글자나 책이 주어이면 '인쇄되다'를 써요. 사람이 프린터로 찍는 것은 '인쇄하다', 보통은 '프린트하다'나 '출력하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The title is printed on the cover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 글자가 찍혀 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe a state where the text is already printed.

phrases.example: 프린터가 고장 나서 인쇄가 안 돼요.
phrases.en: The printer is broken, so nothing prints.
phrases.nuance_ko: 프린터에서 종이가 나오지 않을 때 일상에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when a printer fails to produce pages.

phrases.en: The poster will be printed tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 인쇄될 일을 말하는 미래형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The future form, for something that will be printed.

explain_en: Use 인쇄되다 when the text or book is the subject that gets printed on paper or an object. A person printing with a printer is 인쇄하다, and people often say 프린트하다 or 출력하다 too.

examples.en: When you type a number, it is entered automatically.
My name was entered incorrectly.

examples.ko: 데이터가 모두 입력될 때까지 기다려 주세요.
examples.en: Please wait until all the data is entered.
The characters being entered show on the screen right away.
After the address was entered, the map appeared.
It was entered wrong, so I have to write it again.

explain: 컴퓨터나 폰에 글자, 숫자, 정보가 들어갈 때 써요. 사람이 치면 '입력하다', 저장된 결과를 말하면 '입력되다'예요. 반대말은 '출력되다'이고, 앱 화면에서는 '입력해 주세요'라는 안내를 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: The phone number is entered in my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 들어가 저장된 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where the data has already been entered and saved.

phrases.example: 키보드가 고장 나서 글자가 입력되지 않아요.
phrases.en: The keyboard is broken, so letters aren't being typed in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자나 정보가 들어가지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when letters or information won't go in.

phrases.en: Please check the number you entered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 앱 안내에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies the noun that follows. Often seen in app instructions.

explain_en: Used when letters, numbers or information go into a computer or phone. A person types it with '입력하다'; the stored result is '입력되다'. The opposite is '출력되다' (be output), and apps often show '입력해 주세요' (please enter).

en: to be duplicate; to be repeated

examples.en: The same content is repeated in the application form.

examples.ko: 일정이 중복돼서 한 모임은 못 가요.
examples.en: My schedules overlap, so I can't go to one of the meetings.

examples.ko: 중복된 파일을 지웠더니 용량이 많이 남았어요.
examples.en: After I deleted the duplicate files, a lot of storage was left.

examples.ko: 우리 둘의 설명이 중복되지 않게 나눠서 말해요.
examples.en: The two of us split up what we say so our explanations don't overlap.
The email was duplicated and arrived twice.

examples.ko: 이 목록에는 이름이 중복될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Names may be duplicated in this list.

explain: 같은 것이 두 번 나오거나 겹쳐서 문제가 될 때 써요. '일정이 중복되다', '파일이 중복되다'처럼 써요. 같은 일을 다시 하는 '반복'과 달리 불필요하게 겹친다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Please delete the duplicated content.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겹쳐서 두 번 나온 내용을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for content that appears twice.

phrases.en: Please write them so that no name is duplicated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 것이 두 번 나오지 않게 조심하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to make sure nothing appears twice.

phrases.en: Duplicate applications are not allowed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 것을 두 번 신청하는 일이에요. 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Applying for the same thing twice. Often seen in notices.

explain_en: Use it when the same thing appears twice or overlaps and becomes a problem, as in '일정이 중복되다' (schedules overlap) or '파일이 중복되다' (duplicate files). Unlike '반복' (doing the same thing again), it carries a sense of unnecessary overlap.

examples.ko: 회사에서 새 직원에게 지침서를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: The company handed out a manual to new employees.

examples.ko: 지침서에 안전 규칙이 자세히 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The safety rules are explained in detail in the guidebook.

examples.ko: 처음 쓰는 사람을 위한 지침서를 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I read a guidebook for first-time users.

examples.ko: 지침서대로 하면 실수를 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you follow the guidebook, you can make fewer mistakes.
The school made a new guide for exams.

examples.ko: 이 지침서는 너무 길어서 끝까지 못 읽었어요.
examples.en: This guidebook is so long that I could not read it to the end.

explain: 지침서는 일을 어떻게 해야 하는지 규칙과 순서를 적은 문서예요. 물건 쓰는 법을 적은 '설명서'와 달리, 일하는 방법과 지켜야 할 기준을 적어서 직장이나 기관에서 많이 써요. '매뉴얼'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 공사장에서는 안전 지침서를 꼭 읽어야 해요.
phrases.en: At a construction site, you must read the safety guidelines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전을 위해 지켜야 할 규칙을 적은 문서를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a document of rules to follow for safety.

phrases.en: Please read the manual before you work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 시작하기 전에 확인하라고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when telling someone to check before starting work.

phrases.en: If you work according to the manual, mistakes go down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 기준대로 한다는 뜻으로 '따라'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 따라 to mean following the set standards.

explain_en: 지침서 is a document of rules and steps for how to do a job. Unlike a '설명서', which explains how to use a product, it sets out work methods and standards, so it is common in workplaces and organizations. '매뉴얼' is used in a similar sense.

en: to be integrated; to be unified; to be merged into one

examples.en: The two companies are merged into one.
The apps were integrated into one.
The integrated system is more convenient.
The schools will be merged next year.
Several services are being integrated.
The accounts were merged, so I log in only once.

explain: 따로 있던 것이 하나가 될 때 써요. 회사, 학교, 서비스, 계정 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 짝말은 '분리되다', '나뉘다'예요.

phrases.en: The two classes were combined into one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통합되다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than 통합되다.

phrases.example: 모든 기능이 한 앱에 통합되어 있어요.
phrases.en: All the functions are integrated into one app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 하나로 합쳐진 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of already being integrated.

phrases.en: The two accounts have not been merged yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 하나가 되지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form meaning it hasn't become one yet.

explain_en: Used when separate things become one, as with companies, schools, services and accounts. Its opposite partners are the words for being separated or divided.

en: to retrieve; to recover; to collect

examples.en: The company recalled all the defective products.

examples.ko: 도서관에서 연체된 책을 회수하러 사람을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The library sent someone to collect the overdue books.

examples.ko: 우체통에서 편지를 회수하는 시간이 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: There is a set time when letters are collected from the mailbox.
After collecting the questionnaires, we organize the results.
It isn't easy to recover the money I invested.

examples.ko: 주소가 틀려서 보낸 택배를 다시 회수했어요.
examples.en: The address was wrong, so we took the package back.

explain: 빌려준 물건을 돌려받을 때는 '돌려받다'가 더 일상적이에요. '회수하다'는 불량 제품, 설문지, 투자금처럼 여러 개나 큰 것을 거두어들일 때 많이 써요. 뉴스에서는 '제품 회수', '리콜'과 함께 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I got back the book I lent out today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 빌려준 것을 다시 받을 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday word for getting back something you lent.

phrases.en: I'll collect the questionnaires by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 장을 한꺼번에 거두어들일 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for collecting many sheets at once.

phrases.en: It's hard to recover the money I invested.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 물건을 되찾기 힘들다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is hard to get money or goods back.

explain_en: For getting back something you lent, 돌려받다 is the everyday choice. 회수하다 fits bigger or multiple items, such as defective products, survey forms, or invested money, and it often appears in news about product recalls.

en: to be damaged; to be harmed

examples.en: The old painting was damaged by humidity.
Be careful so that the cultural property is not damaged.

examples.ko: 훼손된 책은 새 책으로 바꿔 드려요.
examples.en: We will exchange a damaged book for a new one.
Once your reputation is damaged, it is hard to recover.
The packaging was damaged, so I returned it.

examples.ko: 자연이 훼손될수록 동물들이 살 곳이 줄어요.
examples.en: The more nature is damaged, the less room animals have to live.

explain: 물건이나 건물이 망가질 때뿐 아니라 '명예', '이미지', '신뢰'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 가치가 나빠질 때도 써요. '망가지다'보다 딱딱해서 법, 뉴스, 안내문에 많아요. 능동은 '훼손하다'예요.

phrases.example: 거짓 소문 때문에 그의 명예가 훼손됐어요.
phrases.en: His honor was damaged because of a false rumor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이지 않는 가치가 나빠질 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for damage to intangible values.

phrases.en: They are restoring the damaged cultural property.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형으로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form often heard in the news.

phrases.example: 벽에 낙서해서 건물을 훼손하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not damage the building by drawing graffiti on the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 망가뜨리는 일은 능동형 '훼손하다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, for a person causing the damage.

explain_en: It covers not only objects and buildings being ruined but also invisible things such as honor, image, and trust being harmed. It is stiffer than '망가지다', so it is common in law, news, and notices. The active form is '훼손하다'.

dis.h: formal: defaced, e.g. heritage or honor

p.n: 손상되다 is the plainer general word for being damaged.
